content.text: Wars and Kingdoms

In Ancient Warfare 2: M&B the factions of the world are living powers. They go to war, make peace and form alliances as the days pass; their leaders rule cities with garrisons; those cities are raided, besieged and conquered. You can swear allegiance to a faction and fight in its wars, or place a Town Hall and found a kingdom of your own.
Every number in this chapter is a default. The server operator can change all of them in the file config/ancientwarfare/AncientWarfareDiplomacy.cfg.
Relations Between Factions

Any two factions are at war, at peace or allied. When a world begins, factions that are hostile to each other by nature are at war. As the days pass (Minecraft days: sleeping and the /time command count) every war wears the two sides down: each death, each lost city and each failed attack adds war exhaustion.
A war that has lasted at least 3 days ends in a truce once the exhaustion is high enough (30). During a truce the two factions cannot declare war on each other. Rivals whose truce is over can fall into war again, and two factions that are at war with the same enemy can become allies, who may then join each other's wars. A faction fights at most 3 wars and has at most 2 alliances.
Only factions that rule at least one city take part in this. Some factions never make peace: Brigands, Pirates, monsters, beasts, the Undead, Demons and vampires.
Cities

A faction leader, the Leader NPC with the golden label “Leader of the …”, rules a city: the area of its structure or town. The city has a name, a garrison (the soldiers of the structure) and manpower, a reserve of soldiers. When a garrison soldier dies a replacement arrives after 30 seconds and costs 1 manpower; a city regains 1 manpower every Minecraft day. A purple bar at the top of the screen shows the manpower of the city you are in.
A city has one ruler, the highest of its leaders; the others are its captains. The ruler and the garrison never despawn. Cities of the same faction that overlap are merged into one.
Raids and Sieges

Factions at war attack each other’s cities, close to players. A raid is a small attack of one or two waves. A siege is rare and large: up to 4 waves of soldiers, archers and cavalry, with siege engines handled by engineers. A faction with no known city can only raid. The size depends on the strength of the city (its garrison and manpower) and on the strength of the attacking faction.
A siege costs the attacking faction one manpower for each attacker, taken from all its cities. A faction always keeps half of its manpower at home: below that it cannot lay sieges, only raid. If the siege fails, only a few of the attackers (up to a fifth) come back; if the city falls, nobody comes back, but the faction gains the city. Raids cost nothing.
When an attack begins a horn sounds and a red bar shows the health of the attackers. They march on the leader of the city, open doors, climb the ladders they place against walls, lay planks over gaps and, in a siege, break through walls. The defenders come out to meet them, and archers on the walls keep shooting. A wave that makes no progress for five minutes retreats and the next one follows.
The attack is over when every wave is beaten off, when peace is made, or when the leader of the city is killed. Then the city is conquered: the old garrison flees, the surviving attackers become the new garrison and a governor of the winners takes the leader’s place. A conquered city starts small and regains its manpower slowly; reinforcements keep arriving until its garrison is as large as it was before.
Joining a Faction

Speak to the Leader of a faction that is not hostile to you (within 8 blocks). A window opens: press “Pledge allegiance to …”. You can belong to one faction at a time.
As a member the enemies of your faction become your enemies (your standing with them falls to at most -100), its allies become friendly (at least 50), and its soldiers are never hostile to you. Your standing with your faction rises to at least 100. When your faction makes peace or war, your standings follow.
To leave, speak to your Leader and choose “Renounce your allegiance” (or use /awmembership leave): a positive standing with the faction returns to 0 and the standings you inherited are given back. Killing a member of your own faction gets you expelled. If your faction loses its last city you are released from your oath without penalty.
Chests of Your Faction

The chests in the structures of your faction stay locked while its soldiers can see you, until you are trusted by it: a standing of 150 or more. Trying to open one before that costs you 5 standing. After your faction conquers a city in a campaign you served in, all the chests of that city are open to you for 10 minutes: the spoils of war.
Protected Structures

Many faction structures have a Protection Flag: a banner in the faction’s colours, with small sun-like particles floating around it. While the flag belongs to the faction, the full blocks and loot chests of the structure take 100 times longer to mine (spawners are not protected, and creative mode is not affected).
To capture the flag, right click it once no hostile NPC is alive in the structure and no spawner is left inside; otherwise the NPC or spawner in the way is marked for a few seconds. A captured flag shows the head of the player who took it, and the structure is no longer protected against that player and his team.
Inside an active city of your own faction (including the cities it conquered, and the cities of your kingdom) you mine normally, whoever holds the flag.
The server operator can turn the protection off or change how much slower it is with block_protection and block_protection_multiplier in config/ancientwarfare/AncientWarfare.cfg.
Military Service

A member is a soldier of the faction. When your faction attacks an enemy city within 1500 blocks, or one of its cities is attacked, you are called to arms: a message gives the city, its distance and its direction, and reminders follow. The army gathers at a point 24 blocks outside the city, on your side of it: the message gives its coordinates. The attack waits for you for 2 minutes plus about 0.3 seconds for each block of the longest journey (at most 30 minutes); when you reach the gathering point, the attack begins. Your own soldiers who follow you join the assault.
You have served if you are at the city when the attack ends or have spent at least a minute there. Serving earns 10 standing, forgives a strike and pays wages (see Coins and Wages); each enemy you kill in the attack gives 1 more standing, up to 10 per attack.
If you do not come, an attack you were called to is cancelled and a city that nobody came to defend is plundered and loses manpower. You get a strike and lose 25 standing for each strike you have (25, then 50); on the third strike you are expelled and lose 50 more. A strike is forgiven after 7 days. Peace during the muster, going offline or an operator stopping the attack excuses you.
Proposing a Campaign

Speak to your Leader and choose “Propose a campaign”: you see the nearest enemy cities and can propose a raid (it needs a standing of 120) or a full siege (180). The Leader refuses if too many attacks are already in progress, if the faction is exhausted by that war, or if you proposed a campaign less than a day ago. If it is accepted, the campaign begins like any other and you are called. If the city holds out, you lose half of the standing that was needed. A full siege is also refused when the levies of your faction are spent (see Raids and Sieges); your own soldiers that join the assault are given back to the faction one for one.
Your Own Kingdom
The Governor

Only you, the owner, see the options of the Governor.
Diplomacy: the factions that rule cities, with your relation to each. You can declare war (it asks for confirmation, and it is not possible during a truce other than the first); propose peace (accepted after 3 days of war if one side is exhausted, never by eternal enemies; a truce follows); propose an alliance (accepted if you and they are at war with the same enemy, outside of a truce); or break an alliance. Peace and alliances are never made for you: only you decide. Other factions can still declare war on you.
The kingdom: your capital, its manpower, your culture, your wars and alliances.
Order a campaign: choose an enemy city and a raid or a siege. Your kingdom never starts attacks on its own: only the campaigns you order. Enemies at war attack your cities from time to time, and every such attack calls you to their defense: gather your soldiers, or the city is plundered. It costs 1 manpower of your capital for each attacker the campaign will have, and it is not refunded if the attack is cancelled. You and your subjects are called to arms as usual, but you never get strikes in your own kingdom.
Manpower, Conquest and Tribute

The manpower of your capital starts at 20, plus 2 for each of your own combat soldiers inside it when you found it. After that, each new combat soldier you place with its item inside a city of your kingdom adds 2 to that city's maximum manpower and 2 to its manpower, and one soldier to the garrison its free reinforcements bring back. Moving soldiers between cities changes nothing, and it never shrinks when they die. Free recruits of your kingdom also arrive in the capital, up to 6 soldiers.
Your kingdom grows in two ways. Place another Town Hall at least 128 blocks from every city of your kingdom (and away from other cities): it founds a new city of the kingdom, with its own Governor and 20 manpower plus 2 for each of your soldiers inside it. Or conquer cities: kill the leader of an enemy city yourself, with your soldiers, or in a campaign you ordered, and the city becomes yours, with your culture. Each city other than the capital pays tribute: half of its maximum manpower is added to the manpower of your capital, which pays the raids of the kingdom. A full siege is paid by all the cities of the kingdom, like for any faction, and your own soldiers that join it are given back one for one. /awkingdom info lists all your cities.
If you lose all your cities, the kingdom ends and you are free again. To end it yourself, use /awkingdom disband confirm: every city of the kingdom is abandoned.
Taxes

Every city collects taxes each Minecraft day while it is not under attack: one Gold Dragon for every 20 points of its maximum manpower, at least one. A city keeps at most 14 days of taxes; a plundered or conquered city loses them all.
The taxes of your kingdom are yours. Speak to the Governor of a city and choose “Collect taxes”: at your capital you collect the taxes of every city of the kingdom, at another city only those of that city. /awkingdom info shows the treasury of each city.
Recruits and Veterans

At the Governor of a city of your kingdom, “Recruit soldiers” hires soldiers of your own: each recruit costs one Gold Dragon and one manpower of that city. Recruits come with the gear of your culture's soldiers and follow you; like all your soldiers they need food.
Soldiers gain levels by fighting; the window of a soldier (right click) shows its level under the order slots, its XP when you point at it, and its tier. “Train my soldiers” shows your soldiers within 16 blocks of the Governor that have earned a promotion: at level 3 a soldier can be trained to tier 2 (the gear of your culture's elite soldiers) for 5 Gold Dragons, at level 6 to tier 3 for 12, which also gives it 10 more maximum health (5 hearts). What it wore before is dropped at its feet. A culture without such gear gives the gear of the config: a wooden sword and a leather helmet, then iron sword and chainmail, then iron sword, shield and iron armor.
When you change the culture, your recruits, trained soldiers and free reinforcements take the gear of their tier in the new culture (the old gear is not dropped; anything else you gave them is). Soldiers in unloaded areas change when they are loaded. Soldiers you placed with their item keep the gear you gave them.
Commanding your soldiers: hold a Command Baton. Right click one of your soldiers to add or remove it; sneak + right click adds all your soldiers within 24 blocks (on one of them, only those of its type), and again clears the group. The soldiers of the group glow for a moment when you select them or give an order. Then press Z to give the order chosen with sneak + scroll: attack, move (on one of your soldiers: guard it), hold position (they fight only what comes close, archers shoot from there), follow me, retreat (they stop fighting and come back to you for 5 seconds), patrol (around the block you look at: they walk around it and fight what they meet), set or clear their home or upkeep, clear their orders. Any order other than follow and retreat makes them stop following you, and soldiers sent somewhere stay there. Any order also takes them out of an assault of the military service. The key can be changed in the controls (Ancient Warfare, alternate item use 1).
Coins and Wages

Ancient Warfare has four coins: the Copper Owl, the Silver Stag, the Gold Dragon and the Ancient Coin. Traders accept them in exchange for their goods, and change them: 9 copper for 1 silver, 1 silver for 7 copper, 9 silver for 1 gold and 1 gold for 7 silver. Eight coins of one metal are worth about one of the next. Eight coins can be placed on the ground as a coin stack.
When you serve in a campaign of your faction, the Leader owes you wages: 3 Gold Dragons for a raid, 8 for a full siege. Speak to your Leader and choose “Collect my wages” (or use /awservice wages). Wages are lost if you leave the faction. Your own kingdom pays you nothing.
Commands for Every Player

/awmembership join (faction)
Swears allegiance to a faction, like the button of its Leader. A Leader of that faction must be within 8 blocks and your standing with it must be 0 or more.

/awmembership leave
Renounces your allegiance: a positive standing with the faction goes back to 0 and the standings you inherited are given back. Not possible for the owner of a kingdom.

/awmembership status
Your faction, your standing with it, your strikes and the calls to arms you have now.

/awservice propose
Lists the enemy cities you can propose a campaign against, with clickable raid and siege choices. You must be near your Leader.

/awservice propose (city id) (raid or siege)
Proposes that campaign to your Leader, who answers in chat.

/awservice wages
Collects the wages your Leader owes you. You must be near your Leader.

/awkingdom info
Your kingdom: its faction id, culture and every city, with manpower, tribute and treasury.

/awkingdom rename (name)
Renames your kingdom (up to 32 characters).

/awkingdom cityname (name)
Renames your capital.

/awkingdom culture (faction)
Changes the culture of your kingdom: the look, soldiers, dialogues and natural rivals of that faction. Your soldiers take the skins of the new culture, and the ones the kingdom equipped (recruits, trained soldiers, free reinforcements) its gear.

/awkingdom disband confirm
Gives up your kingdom: every city of it is abandoned and you leave it.

/awarmy status
Your own soldiers that are taking part in an assault of your faction.
Commands for Operators

/awrelation war, peace or alliance (faction) (faction)
Sets the relation between two factions at once, with an announcement.

/awrelation reset (faction) (faction)
Gives the pair back the relation they have by nature.

/awrelation get (faction) (faction), /awrelation list [faction]
Shows one relation, or every relation set in this world (of one faction).

/awdiplomacy status [faction]
Wars, truces and war exhaustion.

/awdiplomacy day
Runs a diplomatic day at once: truces, new wars, alliances.

/awdiplomacy exhaustion (faction) (enemy) (value)
Sets the war exhaustion of a faction in a war.

/awsettlement list
Every known city, with its id, faction, state and manpower.

/awsettlement info [id]
One city in detail (the one you stand in without an id): bounds, manpower, garrison loaded, leader.

/awsettlement faction [faction]
Without a faction: one line for each faction with cities, with its manpower and whether it can lay sieges. With a faction: its kingdom, manpower kept at home and to spare, every city, its relations with the other factions, its attacks in progress and its members.

/awsettlement setmanpower (id) (amount), /awsettlement rename (id) (name)
Changes the manpower or the name of a city.

/awsiege start (city id) (faction) [raid or siege [force]]
Starts an attack of that faction on the city at once. A full siege is refused when the faction cannot pay it (its levies are spent), unless you add force.

/awsiege stop (city id), /awsiege list
Stops the attack on a city, or lists the attacks in progress with their timers.

/awservice call attack or defend [raid or siege] [player]
Starts a campaign for a member at once: an attack of their faction on a nearby enemy city, or an enemy attack on one of its cities. The player is called to arms.

/awservice strikes (player) (n)
Sets the strikes of a member.

/awmembership set (player) (faction), /awmembership clear (player)
Moves a player into a faction, or out of it.

/awkingdom debugcreate [culture]
Creates a kingdom without a city, for testing.

/awfaction get, set, setall, add or subtract (player) ...
Shows or changes the standing of a player with the factions (from Ancient Warfare 2).
